issues.description: The UML and problem text specify Animal has a constructor Animal(String, int) (name and age), but the provided solution implements Animal(String) with a single String parameter. This mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students about the required constructor signature and how subclasses should call super(...).
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one authoritative design and make all artifacts consistent. Either (A) update the solution and template to implement Animal(String, int): add a private int age, implement Animal(String, int), add getters/setters, and update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) and example Main calls to pass an age; or (B) update the UML/problem text to require only a name (Animal(String)) and remove the age attribute everywhere. Ensure the chosen constructor signature is used consistently in problem_statement.md, template Main/Farm, and the solution classes.

issues.description: The UML/problem description declares an age:int attribute for Animal, but the solution's Animal class has only a name attribute and no age field. This contradicts the explicit UML attributes and the task instructions that mention initializing all class attributes and implementing getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align attributes across specification, template, and solution. Either (A) add the age:int attribute to Animal in the solution and template examples, implement corresponding getter/setter and update constructors/subclasses to initialize age; or (B) remove the age attribute from the UML/problem text so that only name remains. Ensure the final decision is reflected in problem_statement.md, the template code examples, and the reference solution.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with attributes 'name' and 'age' and a constructor Animal(String, int), but both the template usage and the solution implement Animal (and subclasses) with a single-argument constructor taking only name (e.g., Seal/Pig/Goat constructed with a single String). This mismatch in the Animal constructor signature and the presence/absence of the 'age' attribute creates mapping confusion: students following the UML will implement/expect a two-parameter constructor but the provided template main and the solution expect/implement one-parameter constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor and attribute list consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to remove the 'age' attribute and specify Animal(String) as the constructor (so it matches the template Main and the solution), or (B) update the template and solution to include the 'age' attribute and use Animal(String, int) constructors everywhere (and adjust Seal/Pig/Goat construction sites accordingly).
